beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Even a room's floor supplies information through vibrations in the body.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Safety is therefore something they feel before they can explain it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Open space can be frightening where a low ceiling feels reassuring.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel builds its society from those sensory differences, not decorative alien names.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You learn the world by noticing what comforts or alarms its inhabitants.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: At the opening, Sava Ilen is a demographer and a worried sister.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: She works inside the institution that allocates births and scarce resources.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Her partner, Oru Ven, repairs the root network sustaining their city.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their daughter Nemi listens closely to sounds adults often dismiss.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Sava's younger brother Taren notices danger differently from the people around him.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These relationships give the public questions private weight from the first chapter.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An administrative choice can enter the kitchen long before anyone calls it politics.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Taren's training tries to make movement arrive before analysis can interfere.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He instead notices a machine's joints, its sounds and its worn parts.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: His therapist understands that delay through the history of hunted ancestors.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Taren wonders whether the body might recognize something the treatment has missed.
